title: Flat unshaded render mode with globally-unique RGB per patch
description:
Add a second render mode to PatchRenderer that produces a multiview where each patch has a globally-unique, Lambert-free RGB value. The VLM labeler can then pixel-sample this render to deterministically map (x,y) → patch_id, eliminating visual ambiguity where Lambert shading makes two differently-colored patches look similar under grazing light.

Current behavior: PatchRenderer applies Lambert shading ("lambert = 0.5 + 0.5 * |n·L|", clamped to [0.35, 1.0]) to a 20-color palette. Two patches with similar base colors at different lighting angles can look identical to a VLM.

New behavior:
1. Add PatchRenderer.renderMultiviewFlat(mesh, decomposition) that:
   - Assigns each patch a UNIQUE 24-bit RGB value from a generator that guarantees distinct, visually discriminable colors (HSL(golden_ratio_hue, 0.65, 0.55) per pid works well up to ~300 patches).
   - Skips Lambert — every fragment of a face writes its patch's exact RGB.
2. New CLI command 'render-flat' and automation endpoint /mesh/patches/render-flat-multiview.
3. The decomposition JSON already carries per-patch color; the flat-render endpoint emits the same palette mapping so the Python side has (color -> patch_name) lookup.
4. A helper patch_at_pixel(png, x, y) that loads the flat PNG and returns the patch name whose color matches the sampled pixel (exact match; if interior-only to avoid anti-alias seams, use 1-pixel erode).

Use cases:
- VLM labeler: 'for patch_7 please name it — it is the red region visible in Front view near the mandible'. With flat render, the labeler can't confuse adjacent shades.
- Debugging: know exactly which pixel belongs to which patch.
- Future voyage agent self-tagging: the agent renders its own output flat and reads back which of its patches cover the reference's patches.

Originated from PATCH-1+2 follow-up — Welsh-Powell (PATCH-4) covers human viewing; this is its machine-read counterpart.
definition-of-done: renderMultiviewFlat method ships. CLI 'render-flat' subcommand works on the skull. patch_at_pixel helper lands in label_patches.py; it round-trips through a sampled test (pick a pixel near the centroid of each patch, confirm the color matches that patch's unique color).
testing-plan: (1) mvn exec PatchDecomposerCLI render-flat /tmp/skull.obj /tmp/skull.patches-flat.png 128; inspect PNG visually. (2) Python: patch_at_pixel for 5 hand-picked (x,y) points returns the expected patch_id (verify by looking up the face at that pixel via the depth buffer — or by eyeballing on a high-contrast color scheme).
